The updated plan was submitted to the IRB and received a second review and approval in February 2024. 6.1.2.3 Subtask 2.3.0: Pre-Deployment Occupant Recruitment and Experience Expectation Significant pre-deployment planning was conducted for the customer experience baseline assessment. The survey design was carefully crafted to ensure that the information and questions were tailored to the property, including an understanding of the project and how customers perceive that they would be impacted by various aspects of the project. The survey design also considered the time commitment for a survey respondent to ensure that the time commitment was not viewed as a deterrent or barrier to participation in the survey. The survey deployment planning was conducted to provide the highest level of survey awareness and opportunity for resident participation while balancing survey deployment costs. Based on historical tenant engagement knowledge from the property management company, the plan included a mix of digital and physical delivery. Residents that had an email address on file were sent an email link to the survey while those that may not have email or see their emails in a timely manner also had access and awareness of the survey through onsite flyers. In total, the survey was deployed and made available to more than 600 multifamily residents to participate in the survey including notifications through email, posted flyers in common areas, and posted flyers on individual tenant units. Multiple meetings and sessions were also held with commercial property management and owners to discuss the project, interest in project participation, expected goals and objectives from the project, and the baseline operations for the area of the company that would be impacted. 6.1.2.4 Subtask 2.4.0 - Evaluate Consumer Preferences and Make Recommendations The survey and occupant outreach were completed, and the results of the findings were captured in a document for consumer preferences and recommendations. While limited, residents' responses regarding the project reflect a spectrum of expectations and concerns. Many anticipated minimal personal impacts, foreseeing small adjustments in energy usage that may not significantly disrupt their routines. There was some optimism about potential benefits such as cost savings, improved environmental sustainability, and enhanced community amenities like increased parking and better security measures for package deliveries. Some residents were eager for technological advancements like smart home access and advanced lighting controls, viewing these innovations as opportunities to improve efficiency and comfort. Overall, there was excitement about the potential positive outcomes these projects could bring. 6.1.3 Task 3: Develop Cybersecurity Plan and Framework The project team developed a detailed Cybersecurity Plan and framework for the project and provided updates on this plan and framework on a regular cadence as the project progressed. Cybersecurity activities began in 2022 with the development of an initial cybersecurity framework that was discussed and reviewed among the project team. The framework was also evaluated by BHE IT’s cybersecurity office (CSO). An effective Cybersecurity Plan was documented based on the inventory of attack surfaces which can be exploited on our project.
